acceptance_criteria.criterion: The dead cc_model: sharedMeta.cc_model line no longer exists in the context object
The model resolution no longer references sharedMeta.cc_model
The ccModel resolution still checks persona.cc_model before falling back to model

summary: Removed dead `cc_model: sharedMeta.cc_model` from context object (~line 611) — superseded by `...persona` spread and explicit `cc_model: ccModel` below.
Added defensive single-quoting to model fields in all three frontmatter templates: FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_VSCODE, FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_CC, FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC.
Simplified model fallback chain — removed `|| sharedMeta.cc_model` from the ternary; `sharedMeta.default_model || 'inherit'` is now the sole fallback.
Preserved ccModel resolution intact: `persona.cc_model !== undefined ? persona.cc_model : model`.

Rebuilt 34 personas (ledger + standalone, both targets) with `--suite all` — all built cleanly. Generated output shows `model: 'Claude Sonnet 4.6'` for ledger and `model: 'inherit'` for standalone CC personas.

comments.note: The `--suite` CLI flag defaults to `ledger` only; the standard `node scripts/build-personas.js` command silently skips standalone personas. The build header comment (lines 13-15) documents `--suite standalone` and `--suite all`, but it's easy to miss during day-to-day builds. Consider making `--suite all` the default, or at minimum adding a warning when persona output directories already exist for suites not being built.

scripts/build-personas.js carries three separate frontmatter template constants (FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_VSCODE, FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_CC, FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC) that share structurally similar YAML fragments. Fields like `model`, `permissionMode`, and `memory` appear in both CC templates verbatim. As the template count grows, a small template-composition helper would reduce drift risk.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified in source (scripts/build-personas.js). Build passes cleanly — 34 personas built across all suites and targets with no errors. --check flag confirms all 34 output files are up-to-date (no stale output). Rendered output confirms single-quoted model fields: ledger CC/VS Code show 'Claude Sonnet 4.6', standalone CC shows 'inherit'. Dead sharedMeta.cc_model reference confirmed absent from both context object and _shared.yaml. ccModel per-persona escape hatch code path is preserved and correct (no active exercisers in current YAML, not a defect). Edge-case: empty default_model guarded by || 'inherit'.

comments.note: The per-persona cc_model escape hatch (persona.cc_model !== undefined ? persona.cc_model : model) is preserved and correct but has no active exercisers — no persona YAML currently sets cc_model. Consider adding at least one comment noting the intent so future developers don't accidentally remove it as dead code.
No defects — code is clean and consistent across all 6 acceptance criteria points.

summary: Reviewed scripts/build-personas.js against all 6 acceptance criteria. Three surgical changes are correct and complete: (1) dead `cc_model: sharedMeta.cc_model` line is confirmed absent from both the context object and the fallback chain; (2) all three frontmatter templates (FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_VSCODE, FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_CC, FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC) now carry single-quoted model fields; (3) model fallback simplified to `sharedMeta.default_model || 'inherit'` with no stale `sharedMeta.cc_model` reference remaining. Rendered output verified end-to-end across all 17 output files — ledger VS Code shows `model: 'Claude Opus 4.6'` / `model: 'Claude Sonnet 4.6'`, ledger CC mirrors those values correctly, standalone CC uniformly shows `model: 'inherit'`. ccModel per-persona escape hatch (`persona.cc_model !== undefined ? persona.cc_model : model`) is preserved intact. No blocking issues identified.

comments.note: scripts/build-personas.js uses raw string interpolation ({{token}} substitution) for model values in frontmatter — not YAML serialization. If a model string ever contains a single quote (e.g., a future hypothetical 'OpenAI\'s GPT-4'), the YAML output would be malformed. The current model name corpus makes this a non-issue in practice, but worth tracking if the tool ever expands beyond Anthropic model names. Not a regression — pre-existed this PR.

The per-persona cc_model escape hatch (persona.cc_model !== undefined ? persona.cc_model : model, line ~555) is code-correct and well-placed in the build pipeline but is invisible to future developers since no persona YAML currently exercises it. A single-line comment above the ternary (e.g., `// per-persona override for Claude Code; falls back to the common model value`) would make the intent explicit and prevent accidental removal during future refactors. Echoes the QA observation — not a blocking defect.

No blocking issues — code is minimal, correct, and consistent with existing template patterns. The asymmetry between FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_VSCODE (no model field) and FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC (model: '{{cc_model}}') is intentional and architecturally sound: VS Code prompt frontmatter does not support model selection; Claude Code agent YAML does.

Updated personas/docs/agents/project-manifest/data-flows.md: removed dead cc_model: _shared.cc_model from Layer 1 of the Merge Context Details; added cc_model as a Layer 3 computed value with comment 'persona.cc_model ?? model — all CC targets'.

Updated personas/docs/agents/project-manifest/constraints.md: rewrote constraint 28c to show the simplified cc_model resolution chain (persona.cc_model → persona.model → sharedMeta.default_model → 'inherit'), updated template reference to single-quoted form, and removed legacy _shared.cc_model fallback explanation paragraph.

Consider adding an inline comment in build-personas.js near the ccModel computation to note this is an intentional escape hatch, preventing future developers from removing it as dead code.
